newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 3.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - "The Empire Strikes Back" by News Corp's 20th Century Fox led the weekend with about $12.6 million, but "Donnie Brasco" released by Sony Corp's TriStar was right behind with $11.2 million. Together, along with $6.4 million from "Booty Call," also released by Sony, the frame sped along to around $80 million, 20 percent ahead of the comparable weekend last year.

* HOLLYWOOD - Steven Soderbergh will direct George Clooney in "Out of Sight," by Seagram's Universal Pictures, sources said. The picture is being produced by Jersey Films' Michael Shamberg, Danny DeVito and Stacey Sher.
* HOLLYWOOD - Mark Damon's MDP Worldwide and veteran indie producer Moshe Diamant unveiled on Saturday a $35 million picture called "Knock Off" featuring action star Jean-Claude Van Damme.

* HOLLYWOOD - Congressman Billy Tauzin, chairman of the House Telecommunications Subcommittee, told Hollywood executives that it may be time to revisit the debate over the now-defunct financial interest and syndication rules. Eliminated by the Federal Communications Commission in 1993, the financial interest and syndication rules prevented networks from owning much of their primetime programming and kept them out of the domestic syndication business entirely. Removal of the rules led to the merger of Disney and ABC, the launching of networks by Time Warner and Viacom's Paramount and the expansion into production by Westinghouse's CBS and General Electric's NBC.

* HOLLYWOOD - The 1997 Los Angeles Independent Film Festival (April 3-7) features 16 world premieres among its 20 films, three feature documentaries and 34 shorts. Presented by the Sundance Channel and the Filmmakers Foundation, the fest takes place at Raleigh Studios and Paramount Studios except for opening and closing nights at the Directors Guild of America, a founding sponsor along with Raleigh and Kodak.

* LAS VEGAS - Twentieth Century Fox's fabulously successful re-releases of "Star Wars" and "The Empire Strikes Back" propelled first-quarter box office to record highs. Largely on the coattails of those films, the overall national box office for the year hit the $1 billion mark over the weekend, the earliest that milestone has been reached.
